## Rule

task385 = ARC-GEN **f25ffba3**. **Vertical symmetric reflection**: the input has colored bars rising from the bottom of a **10-row × 4-col** active grid; the output mirrors the bottom half onto the top half so the active grid becomes symmetric about the horizontal line between rows 4 and 5. Quadruple-confirmed (2026-05-31):
1. Generator `external/ARC-GEN/tasks/task_f25ffba3.py`: input `grid[2H-1-r][col]=color` (fills from bottom row 9 up); output `output[r][col]=output[2H-1-r][col]=color` (sets BOTH top row `r` and bottom row `2H-1-r`), with H=5 ⇒ 2H=10. Net per-row map: `output[r]=input[9-r]` for r∈0..4; `output[r]=input[r]` for r∈5..9; identity on padding tail rows 10..29.
2. Shipped `v0 = [9,8,7,6,5, 5,6,7,8,9, 10,11,…,29]` (extracted from `submission.zip` 2026-05-31) literally encodes that map. opset 10, ir 8.
3. ORT byte-check: LIVE Gather == numpy `input[:,:,idx,:]` on **2000/2000** random full one-hots.
4. `verify_against_live --tid 385`: Prototype(rebuilt) vs LIVE **265/265** visible+arc-gen.

ONNX = a single `Gather(input, v0, axis=2)`. Output is the graph output (free). cost = memory(0) + params(30) = **30** → 21.5988 pts. **This is the hard floor (proof below); already held by LIVE.**

## Algorithm sketch

```
output[:, :, j, :] = input[:, :, idx[j], :]   for j in 0..29
idx = [9,8,7,6,5, 5,6,7,8,9, 10,11,…,29]       # top half = mirror of bottom; tail identity
# closed form (verified 2026-06-01): idx[r] = max(r, 9-r) for ALL r in 0..29
#   (the fold around row-4.5 for r≤9, identity for r≥10 — single expression, but still a 30-element non-monotonic permutation)
```
Pure row-reorder along axis 2 — zero MACs, zero arithmetic, no intermediate tensors. Note every `idx` value ≥ 5 (input rows 0–4 are never read), and the block `[9,8,7,6,5,5,6,7,8,9]` is **numpy `symmetric` mode** (edge repeated), NOT ONNX `reflect` (edge omitted).

## Cost analysis — FLOOR PROOF (cost 30 is the hard floor)

**Theorem.** For task385 — and for any same-shape axis-2 (row) permutation/fold on `[1,10,30,30]` whose output-row map is **non-monotonic** (not a single strided slice) — the minimum cost through the official `neurogolf_utils` scorer is exactly **H = 30**, realized by a single dense-index `Gather(input, idx, axis=2)`.

**Setup (from scorer source — identical accounting to task337).** `cost = memory + params`.
- `params` = Σ element counts of initializers / Constant values (**dtype-agnostic**; int8/uint8/fp16 packing saves 0).
- `memory` = Σ over every node-output / value_info tensor **except** the two named `input`/`output`, of `num_elements × dtype.itemsize` (**bytes**).
- Exactly one input (`input` [1,10,30,30] F32) and one output (`output` [1,10,30,30]); both free; multi-IO rejected. `output ≠ input` (rows 0–4 differ).

**Lemma 1 — no usable intermediate is affordable.** Any tensor other than `input`/`output` that the graph needs to carry information toward a correct output is either (i) a grid block — minimum useful per-channel row slice `[1,10,1,30]` = 300 elements ⇒ ≥ 300 B even in 1-byte dtype, full `[1,k,30,30]` ≥ 900 B; or (ii) a `[30]` Gather index built on the fly = ≥ 120 B (INT32) / 240 B (INT64). Both ≫ 30, so a cost-≤29 graph can contain **no** such intermediate. *(Empirical: Slice+Concat 36,007; Gather10+Concat 36,013; Gather10+Pad 12,019 — the `[1,10,k,30]` intermediate dominates every time.)*

**Lemma 2 — the last op must read `input` directly.** The op emitting `output` takes operand(s); by Lemma 1 none may be a data/index intermediate; the only free data tensor is `input`. Hence `output` is produced by a **single op reading `input`** (plus tiny/param operands). ⇒ any sub-30 graph is one op, `input → op → output`.

**Lemma 3 — among single ops, only Gather is both correct and cheap, and its index is length 30.** Exhaustive op enumeration for a same-shape axis-2 fold:
- *Identity/Cast* → identity. ✗ wrong.
- *Slice* (incl. opset-10 `steps`) → `output[i]=input[start+i·step]`, a **monotonic** arithmetic sequence; target idx `[9,8,7,6,5,5,6,…]` is non-monotonic ⇒ impossible in one Slice. (Only step=+1 [identity] or −1 [full reverse [29..0]] yield 30 elements; both wrong.) ✗
- *Pad* (constant/reflect/edge/wrap) → only adds/crops at edges; cannot replace interior rows 0–4 with a mirror of rows 5–9. Target `output[0]=input[9]`, but Pad's top fill draws only on rows adjacent to the edge (reflect→1,2,…; edge→row0; wrap→29,28,…), never row 9. **Empirically all 16 mode×config combos = 0/300** (cost 8–9 — cheap but incorrect ⇒ 0 pts). ONNX has no `symmetric` (edge-repeated reflect) mode. ✗
- *Transpose* → whole-axis permutation; a within-axis-2 fold needs a prior Reshape of axis-2 into (a,b) = a `[1,10,a,b,30]` intermediate ≥ 9000 B (Lemma 1). ✗
- *Resize/Upsample* → output→input coordinate map is affine per fixed scale; the target map is non-affine. ✗
- *DepthToSpace/SpaceToDepth* → fixed block shuffle (needs exact shape factors), not an arbitrary fold. ✗
- *ReverseSequence* → banned ("Sequence" substring) + ORT `time_axis∈{0,1}` only (rows are axis 2) + reverses a prefix not a fold. ✗
- *GatherElements/ScatterElements/ScatterND* → cannot beat 30. GatherElements/ScatterElements need a full-output `[1,10,30,30]` index = 9000 params. ScatterND patching only the 5 changed rows (input stays free) was **measured 2026-06-01 at cost 6154**: the row-across-channel index `[1,10,5,3]` is **150 params > 30 by itself**, and the reversed-rows `updates` block `[1,10,5,30]` is an irreducible 6000-B F32 intermediate (can't narrow dtype — must match `input`'s F32). ✗
- *MatMul/Gemm/Conv/Einsum* with a row-permutation operand → weight ≥ `[30,30]` = 900 params, AND a Transpose to place axis 2 ⇒ intermediate. ✗
- ***Gather(input, idx, axis=2)*** → the unique op that directly emits an axis-2-permuted `[1,10,30,30]` and the only one expressing the non-monotonic fold. Output axis size 30 ⇒ `idx.shape[0] = output.shape[2] = 30` ⇒ dense init = **30 params** ⇒ cost = 0 + 30 = **30**. ✓

**Lemma 4 — the sparse escape is rejected AND saves nothing here.** The only way a length-30 index counts <30 params is a `sparse_initializer` (counts NNZ). Two independent kills:
- (a) **NNZ = 30 regardless.** Every `idx` value ≥ 5 (input rows 0–4 never read) ⇒ zero zero-valued entries ⇒ sparse stores all 30 ⇒ no saving even before rejection. *(Strictly stronger than task337, where `idx[0]=0` would have given NNZ=9.)*
- (b) **Rejected at the same 3 gates as task337** (verified 2026-05-31, `score_network_v2 → None`): `onnx.checker.check_model(full_check=True)` ("Gather indices … unsupported type sparse_tensor"), `shape_inference(strict_mode=True)` rank mismatch, `sanitize_model` dangling-rename. ORT densifies+runs (output correct) but the model never scores. Unscored = 0 pts ≪ 21.5988.

**Lemma 5 — exploit-immunity (the floor survives the known scorer accounting gaps).** Verified 2026-06-01 against `Onnx_Advanced/scoring_internals.md`. The documented sub-cost exploits collapse **memory** of *shape-inferred* tensors (dynamic `dim_param`→0, kq5y `ConstantOfShape` data-derived shape, the "positive-cost wrapper" Hacks 1/3) or affect **MACs** (negative-step `Slice` off-by-one — and MACs were removed from scoring 2026-05-04). **None touch `params`**, because `calculate_params` reads `init.dims` / Constant `value.dims` **directly from the proto** (no shape inference, no profiler). The non-monotonic fold requires a 30-element *literal* index; that literal is charged 30 params whether it lives in an `initializer` **or** a `Constant` node (`calculate_params` sums both). Empirical (2026-06-01): routing the index through a runtime `Identity` intermediate scored **(0, 240, 30) = cost 270** (source init still 30 params **+** a 240-B `[30]` INT64 intermediate); `Constant`-node index = **(0, 240, 30) = 270** likewise. Even applying the (owner-forbidden) `dim_param` collapse to that intermediate only zeroes the 240 B → back to **exactly 30**, never below. ∴ no legitimate *or* exploit path beats 30. **Owner stance (this repo, reaffirmed): ethical play only — do not implement accounting-gap wrappers; "we're clean by construction."**

**Conclusion.** By Lemmas 1–3 every scorer-valid **and correct** graph has cost ≥ 30, achieved by the dense Gather; by Lemma 4 the sole sub-30 accounting path (sparse) is rejected and would not even reduce NNZ here; by Lemma 5 the floor is immune to the known cost-metric exploits (they collapse memory/MACs, not the literal-index `params`). **∴ 30 is the hard floor for task385. ∎**

### Why task385's floor (30) > task337's floor (10)
Same proof skeleton, different gathered axis. task337 permutes the **channel** axis (size C=10) ⇒ |idx|=10 ⇒ floor 10. task385 folds the **row** axis (size H=30) ⇒ |idx|=30 ⇒ floor 30. The one cheap structural escape (task337's exact channel-reversal → `Slice(steps=-1)` cost 4) requires a **monotonic** index; this fold is non-monotonic, and the reflection is numpy-`symmetric` (no ONNX `reflect` match). The identity tail `[10..29]` cannot be dropped: Gather replaces the whole axis, and any Slice/Concat reassembly that preserves it carries a ≥12,000 B intermediate (measured).

### Generalization (axis-2 / axis-3 spatial folds)
For any task whose rule is a same-shape spatial-axis permutation on `[1,10,30,30]` along axis 2 (rows) or axis 3 (cols) with a **non-monotonic** index, the floor is the axis length (**30**) via one dense Gather — UNLESS the index is a pure monotonic strided pattern. **Quick test for any axis-2/3 reshuffle:** `idx==range(30)` ⇒ identity (cost 0); `idx==range(29,-1,-1)` ⇒ full reverse ⇒ `Slice(steps=-1)` cost 4 (spatial analogue of task337's reversal exception); **else (any fold/partial reflection) ⇒ Gather floor 30**. task385's idx is a fold ⇒ floor 30; no sub-30 exists.

## Don't-do log

Ruled out (empirically + by proof, 2026-05-31 — do not retry):
- **Any Slice/Concat reassembly** (preserve identity tail; reverse-block + tail; etc.) — every `[1,10,k,30]` intermediate is 1,200·k bytes ≫ 30. Measured 12,019 / 36,007 / 36,013.
- **Gather-10 + Pad-zero-tail** — exploits output rows 10–29 = padding(0); on-distribution-correct (500/500 active) but the `[1,10,10,30]` Gather intermediate = 12,000 B; cost fails before correctness matters. Also 0/2000 on full one-hots (tail not zero off-distribution).
- **Single Pad, any mode** — reflect/edge/wrap/constant × {±5,±10}: all cost 8–9 (**cheap!**) but 0/300 correct. Pad cannot place `input[9]` at `output[0]`; ONNX has no `symmetric` mode. The cheap cost is a **trap** — incorrect ⇒ literal 0 pts.
- **ReverseSequence** — banned ("Sequence" substring) + ORT `time_axis∈{0,1}` only + wrong semantics.
- **sparse_initializer Gather index** — rejected at 3 gates (checker/shape-infer/sanitize); AND NNZ=30 here (no zero values) so it saves nothing even in principle.
- **Smaller index dtype (int8/uint8/fp16)** — `params` counts ELEMENTS not bytes; 30 either way.
- **Constant node for the index** — counts 30 params AND adds a counted `[30]` intermediate (+≥120 B). Worse than a plain dense initializer.
- **Crop-to-active-grid (10×4)** — the crop intermediate `[1,10,10,4]` = 1,600 B F32 (400 B BOOL) already exceeds 30; crop helps only high-cost baselines, never a memory-0 floor (same verdict as task337 crop-skip).
- **MatMul/Conv/Gemm row-permutation matrix** — ≥ [30,30]=900 params + a Transpose intermediate.
- **ScatterND partial-row patch** (keep `input` free, overwrite only rows 0–4) — measured 2026-06-01 = cost **6154**. The "input is free so only pay for the 5 changed rows" intuition fails twice: (a) addressing 5 rows across all 10 channels costs a `[1,10,5,3]`=150-element index → already > 30; (b) the moved pixel values are F32 and the `updates` `[1,10,5,30]`=6000-B tensor can't be narrowed without a dtype mismatch vs `input`. Same verdict for ScatterElements (index ≥1500).

**Recommendation: close the sub-floor hunt for task385. cost 30 = hard floor, already held by LIVE. Nothing to ship (captain ships; LIVE is already optimal). This is the axis-2 analogue of the task337 recolor-floor proof. Re-confirmed independently 2026-06-01 (ground-truth scorer source + `ng_gate` byte-equal + corrected ScatterND measurement); the floor stands.**
